findings.governingReading: Sakura is asked to scrape away the sardine’s belly bones.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a central spine-like bone.

findings.highlight: We’ll cook it after you’re done
findings.governingReading: They will grill the sardines after Sakura removes the belly bones.
findings.explanation: The English omits the specific remaining task.

findings.evidenceJa: サラダ油をこさじ半分ほど
findings.governingReading: Shirou adds approximately half a teaspoon of cooking oil.
findings.explanation: The English drops both oil type and measured quantity.

findings.evidenceJa: フライパンを持つ手が止まった
findings.governingReading: The hand holding the frying pan freezes at Sakura’s question.
findings.explanation: The English omits the pan that makes the reaction visible and potentially risky.

findings.highlight: I’m sure Sakura didn’t see my disturbance
findings.evidenceJa: 伝わらなかっただろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou supposes his one-instant reaction probably did not register with Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens probability and narrows perception to sight.

findings.governingReading: Rin thumps down and roughly claims her place.
findings.explanation: The English invents a shambling gait and omits her forceful occupation of the seat.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka and Illya sit across from us
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂とイリヤが隣り合う
findings.governingReading: The text establishes two adjacent pairs without explicitly stating that the pairs face each other.
findings.explanation: The English invents the across-table relation.

findings.evidenceJa: 被害者のものと思われる遺体の一部
findings.governingReading: Police reportedly find part of a body thought to belong to the victim.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes victims before the report establishes the possible count.

findings.highlight: I’m sure this was an unforeseen accident
findings.evidenceJa: 事故だったんじゃないかしら
findings.governingReading: Rin tentatively proposes an unforeseen accident as her preferred explanation.
findings.explanation: The English promotes the hypothesis into certainty.

findings.highlight: omelet is gone as she speaks
findings.evidenceJa: 卵焼きはとっくになくなっている
findings.governingReading: Rin’s own omelet has long since been eaten before she offers the wager.
findings.explanation: The English suggests it becomes gone during her speech.

findings.highlight: there was four of something people only have one of
findings.evidenceJa: 一つしかない筈のものが四つ
findings.governingReading: Rin posits four examples of a body part each person should possess only once.
findings.explanation: The English uses singular “was” with four objects and awkwardly attaches the relative clause.

findings.governingReading: Such shapes could establish victim count even before forensic examination.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes identification of persons for forensic analysis of evidence.
